balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Smoore International Holdings Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Smoore International Holdings Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Smoore International Holdings Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Smoore International Holdings Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Smoore International Holdings Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Smoore International Holdings Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Smoore International Holdings Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Smoore International Holdings Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenueCustomerMix.title: Revenue by customer type & product line
revenueCustomerMix.content:
Self-branded is revenue from Smoore's own vapour brands (e.g. VEEV); corporate/ODM clients is contract manufacturing for third-party brands including PMI/IQOS and the major US and international vape brands; heat-not-burn is the newer non-vaping product line.

For Smoore International Holdings Limited: corporate/ODM is the larger and faster-growing line (RMB9,323.6m FY2024 -> RMB11,344.4m FY2025) but typically carries thinner margins than self-branded; heat-not-burn is small but grew roughly 5.8x year on year (RMB223.6m -> RMB1,286.5m) as Smoore diversifies beyond vaping into a product category outside the US flavour-ban fight. Only disclosed in the FY2024 and FY2025 annual reports, so this chart is FY-only and two points wide.

What to watch:

  • Whether corporate/ODM concentration in a small number of brand customers increases counterparty risk
  • Heat-not-burn's share of revenue as a hedge against US vaping regulation
  • Margin mix shift as ODM share grows relative to higher-margin self-branded sales

revenueGeoMix.title: Revenue by geography
revenueGeoMix.content:
Revenue split by the three geographies Smoore discloses: US, Europe & other and China. The remainder of total Revenue is unallocated/other markets not broken out in the filings.

For Smoore International Holdings Limited: the US is the single largest disclosed market (RMB4.4-4.6bn in FY2024-FY2025) and the one most exposed to FDA flavour-ban and PMTA enforcement risk; Europe & other is larger still and growing faster (RMB7.1bn -> RMB9.4bn); China is a small fraction of group revenue despite Smoore being a Chinese manufacturer, since most output is exported. Only disclosed in the FY2024 and FY2025 annual reports, so this chart is FY-only and two points wide.

What to watch:

  • US revenue trend against FDA enforcement and flavour-ban headlines
  • Europe & other's growth rate versus the US, since regulatory risk differs sharply by region
  • Any shift toward China as domestic demand develops

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Smoore International Holdings Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Smoore International Holdings Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
